paper.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Online Fair Division with Bandit Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown means under proportionality in expectation (normalized values)
unmapped: Arms are the n players (K = n); contexts are m item types drawn uniformly at random (M_ctx = m)
Learner chooses a fractional allocation matrix X^t (randomized assignment per item type) before observing the type
Proportionality-in-expectation constraint X_i . mu_i >= 1/n must hold for every player at every round w.h.p.
Player value rows are normalized: sum_k mu_ik = 1; means in known [a,b] with a>0
Regret is against the best proportional allocation Y^{mu*} with known means
settings.definition_quote: there are $N = [n]$ players and $M = [m]$ item types, with $T$ items arriving over time. For any item of type $k$, the value of player $i$ for that item is drawn from a sub-Gaussian distribution with mean $\mu^*_{ik}$. ... we assume that for all players $i$, $\sum_{k=1}^m \mu_{ik}^* = 1$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown means under envy-freeness in expectation (normalized values) (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are players, contexts are uniformly random item types
Envy-freeness-in-expectation constraint must hold at every round w.h.p.
Regret against best envy-free allocation with known means
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm $\alg$ that uses fractional allocation $X^t$ at time $t$ satisfies \emph{envy-freeness in expectation} if for all $t < T$ and all $i \in [n]$, $(X_t)_i \cdot \mu^*_i \ge \max_{i' \in [n]} (X_t)_{i'} \cdot \mu^*_i$.

algorithms.name: UCB Online Fair Division (Algorithm 1) / Fair Upper-Confidence-Bound (Algorithm 2)

conditions: 0 < a <= mu*_ik <= b with a, b known
constraints (proportionality in expectation) also satisfied at every round on the same event
tuning: warm-up of log^2(T) sqrt(T) uniform-at-random rounds

source.label: thm:sqrtT_regret
source.quote: Suppose $n,m, T, a,b$ are known and that the true mean values satisfy $0 < a \le \mu^*_{ik} \le b$ for all $i \in [n]$, $k \in [m]$. With probability $1-1/T$, Algorithm \ref{algo:UCB} will both satisfy the proportionality in expectation constraints for $\mu^*$ and have regret for $\mu^*$ of $\tilde{O}(n^5m^3\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: K = n players, M_ctx = m item types. Hidden dependence on b/a (C_P = bn/a) is suppressed in the stated bound. Runtime stated exponential in n and m. Proof also uses 'sufficiently large T'.

symbols.K_lip: Lipschitz constant K of the constraint map B_l(mu) (Property A.5)

conditions: general linear fairness constraints {(B_l(mu), c_l)} satisfying Properties A.2-A.5
probability 1 - 1/T; constraints satisfied on same event

source.label: lemma:general_sqrtT_regret
source.quote: Suppose $\left\{\{(B_\ell(\mu), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\right\}_{\mu \in [a,b]^{n \times m}}$ satisfy Properties ... Then with probability $1-1/T$, Algorithm \ref{algo:UCB} satisfies the constraints $\{(B_\ell(\mu^*), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}$ and has regret of $\tilde{O}(KC_{\mathrm{P}\ref{def:continuous_app}} C_{\mathrm{P}\ref{def:fairness_to_UAR2_app}}n^3m^3\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: General version of Theorem 3.1 for fairness constraints satisfying the stated properties; recorded under the proportionality setting since that is the instantiation in the paper.

conditions: values Gaussian with variance 1, rows normalized
no algorithm can, for all such mu*, both satisfy envy-freeness in expectation and have regret < T^{2/3}/log T with probability at least 1 - 1/T

source.label: thm:lower_bounds
source.quote: There exists $a,b,n,m$ such that no algorithm can, for all $\mu^* \in [a,b]^{n \times m}$ with rows that add to $1$, both satisfy the envy-freeness in expectation constraints and achieve regret of less than $\frac{T^{2/3}}{\log(T)}$ with probability at least $1-1/T$.

results.notes: Joint constraint-satisfaction/regret impossibility; the lower bound is on the event of both properties holding w.p. >= 1-1/T.
